drugs.name: Isoniazid
drugs.mechanism: Prodrug activated by mycobacterial catalase-peroxidase (katG), then blocks mycolic acid synthesis; bactericidal. Resistance: katG mutation. Structurally similar to pyridoxine.
drugs.adverseEffects: Peripheral neuritis from impaired vitamin B6 activation (prevent with pyridoxine 10-50 mg/day); hepatotoxicity from CYP2E1 metabolites, worse with alcohol, rifampin and pyrazinamide; lupus in slow acetylators
drugs.use: Backbone of active TB therapy for all 6 months; taken alone daily for 9 months as one latent TB option; every prescription includes vitamin B6

drugs.name: Rifampin
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase; resistance from an altered polymerase. Daily dosing; a strong CYP3A4 inducer; distributes widely into body fluids; covers gram-positive, gram-negative and acid-fast bacteria
drugs.adverseEffects: Red-orange urine, tears and saliva (harmless once blood is excluded; shows adherence); hepatitis, worse with isoniazid or pyrazinamide; induces CYP3A4, so oral contraceptives and HIV drugs fail
drugs.use: Four-drug TB therapy, then continued 4 more months; 4 months alone for latent TB; prophylaxis for close contacts of meningococcal or H. influenzae disease (dorm, jail), not meningitis treatment

drugs.name: Rifabutin
drugs.mechanism: Same RNA polymerase target and red secretions as the parent rifamycin, but much weaker CYP induction; hepatotoxicity similar; reduce the dose when CrCl is below 30 mL/min
drugs.use: Replaces the standard rifamycin in TB patients taking antiretroviral therapy, to avoid induction interactions; optional third drug for MAC in advanced HIV

drugs.name: Rifapentine
drugs.mechanism: Rifamycin RNA polymerase inhibitor with a long half-life that allows once-weekly dosing; still a potent CYP inducer
drugs.use: Weekly with isoniazid for 3 months as a latent TB option in HIV (CD4 < 200); part of the newer 4-month active TB regimen with isoniazid, pyrazinamide and moxifloxacin

drugs.name: Pyrazinamide
drugs.mechanism: Prodrug: mycobacterial pyrazinamidase (pncA gene) makes pyrazinoic acid, which lowers intracellular pH and disrupts membranes and fatty acid synthesis; bactericidal on replicating bacilli. Resistance: pncA mutation
drugs.adverseEffects: Marked hepatotoxicity (mitochondrial oxidative stress), additive with isoniazid and rifampin; hyperuricemia from reduced uric acid excretion, which can flare gout
drugs.use: Only the first 2 months (8 weeks) of active TB therapy, then stopped; left out of the pregnancy regimen

drugs.name: Ethambutol
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits mycobacterial arabinosyl transferase (encoded by emb), disrupting the cell envelope; bacteriostatic. Resistance: emb gene mutation
drugs.adverseEffects: Optic neuritis with loss of red-green color discrimination (patients report any vision change); hyperuricemia from increased renal uric acid recovery, which can flare gout
drugs.use: Fourth drug of the 2-month intensive TB phase and kept in the pregnancy regimen; partner to a macrolide for MAC in advanced HIV; also treats M. kansasii
